Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D plus probiotic co-supplementation lowered Beck Depression Inventory scores compared with placebo in women with PCOS.
Sentence: "Vitamin D and probiotic co-supplementation, compared with the placebo, significantly improved beck depression inventory [β (difference in the mean of outcomes measures between treatment groups) - 0.58; 95% CI, - 1.15, - 0.02; P = 0.04], general health questionnaire scores (β - 0.93; 95% CI, - 1.78, - 0.08; P = 0.03) and depression, anxiety and stress scale scores (β - 0.90; 95% CI, - 1.67, - 0.13; P = 0.02)."
Measured as: beck depression inventory score
Population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome aged 18-40 years
Intervention: 50,000 IU vitamin D every 2 weeks plus 8 × 10^9 CFU/day probiotic for 12 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 60
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
